title: feat(spec): a field declares the key(s) it was renamed from — `renamedFrom` on FieldSchema
body:
Fixes #30880

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: added
Skills-docs: follow-up #30885 — `skills/**` does not teach the key yet: it is declared ahead of the upgrade step that carries the data (rename execution, #30885), and that step owns the skills line; this diff documents it in `content/docs/data-modeling/fields.mdx` and the generated references

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:字段定义新增可选属性 `renamedFrom: string[]`,包作者在新字段上写旧名(如 `renamedFrom: ['company']`),并加五条最小校验(旧名须合法、不能是自己、不能和本对象现存字段重名、不能被两个字段同时认领、列表内不重复),违者在解析时拒收并点名对象、字段和旧名。
- 为什么改:按你在 cloud#3652 的裁决(Q3「默认拒绝，需显式映射（推荐）」与「写进清单 renamedFrom」),改名映射写在清单里;这推翻了 #24443 裁决 A 第 5 条「规范里不加改名写法」。本 PR 只做协议这一层,真正搬数据的是 #30885,升级预览读它是 #30884。
- 风险与回滚:不写这个键的对象解析结果不变;`FieldSchema` 是严格模式,带 `renamedFrom` 的制品会被比本版本旧的运行时拒收(未知键)。在 #30885 落地前,这个键不会让任何升级搬数据。回滚即还原本 PR。
- 先看:`packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts`(`refuseDishonestRenamedFrom`,四条整表校验)、`packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts`(新键与 describe 文案)、`packages/spec/liveness/field.json`(`planned` 行与翻转条件)。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run src/data/field-renamed-from.test.ts`,预期 11 个用例全绿。
- 需要你做的:无,席位落地(落地前席位先做一次契约复核)。

## What changes

- **`FieldSchema.renamedFrom: string[]`, optional** (`packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts`, at the tail of the shape so the abbreviated type summaries in the references do not move). Each entry is an earlier key of the same field, in the field-key grammar `^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*$`; a non-key entry is refused by `FieldSchema` itself with a message naming the entry. The `.describe()` says what the key means, that it is read only at package upgrade, and that it is declared ahead of the upgrade step that carries the data.
- **`refuseDishonestRenamedFrom`** in `ObjectSchema`'s `superRefine`, beside `refuseStageFieldWithoutKinds` (`packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts`). One located `custom` issue at `fields.FIELD.renamedFrom.INDEX` per offending entry, naming the object, the field and the old key, when the entry is the field's own key, repeats an earlier entry of the same list, is a key another field of the object still declares, or is an old key an earlier field already claims (reported on the later claimant, naming the first). The own-key and repeat checks sit here rather than in `FieldSchema` because `FieldSchema.name` is optional (the map key is the field's key) and because the card asks every refusal to name the object.
- **Liveness:** `renamedFrom` is a `planned` row in `packages/spec/liveness/field.json`, naming #30885 (rename execution) as the reader that flips it to `live` with its `file#symbol` pointer, and #30884 (upgrade plan) as a second reader. No `authorWarn`, as the card states. `liveness/state-counts/field.md` regenerated.
- **Mirrors the gates require:** the authorable-surface shard (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, +1 row), the generated references (`content/docs/references/**`), the field-form omission ledger (`metadata-form-zod-reconciliation.test.ts`: not offered in the field form while `planned`, the `conditionalFormatting` precedent), the two maps pinned exhaustive over `FieldSchema` (`FIELD_KEY_STORAGE_CLASS` in driver-sql as `storage`; `FIELD_REFERENCE_POSITIONS` in metadata-core as `keep`, since the parse refuses any entry naming a live field), and the `/meta/types` field property count pin (82 to 83).
- **Docs:** one row under a new "Package upgrades" heading in `content/docs/data-modeling/fields.mdx`.
- **Changeset:** `@objectstack/spec` minor, `@objectstack/driver-sql` and `@objectstack/metadata-core` patch.

Not added, per the card: an object-level or package-level rename map, renames of objects or other metadata types, type compatibility checking (the upgrade plan judges it against the installed version), and any runtime behaviour.

### Rulings this lands

- Epic objectstack-ai/cloud#3652, maintainer rulings (record on the epic): Q3 「默认拒绝，需显式映射（推荐）」, and on where the mapping lives, 「写进清单 renamedFrom」.
- These supersede item 5 of objectstack#24443's ruling A (record 6259332195): "No rename spelling is added to the spec". Items 1 to 4 of that record stand. The card notes that no ADR text forbids the key (ADR-0126's dated note describes the access stages, it is not a rule), so no ADR amendment rides here.

### Publish-time consequence, for the contract review

`FieldSchema` is strict. An artifact that carries `renamedFrom` is refused, as an unrecognized key, by every runtime older than this release. A package that adds the key therefore needs its installing runtime at this release or later; a package that does not write it is unaffected. The changeset says the same.

## Tests

- New `packages/spec/src/data/field-renamed-from.test.ts` (11 cases): one and two earlier keys parse and are kept as written; an object without the key parses with no `renamedFrom` materialized on any field; four grammar refusals at `renamedFrom.0`; each of the four map-half refusals pinned by `code` and `path` and by its sentence (object, field, old key, reason clause).
- `os validate` acceptance, run by hand with the built CLI against two throwaway `defineStack` fixtures (removed after): `renamedFrom: ['company']` exits 0; `renamedFrom: ['status']` beside a live `status` field exits 1 with `objects.0.fields.account_name.renamedFrom.0: Field account_name on object crm_account declares renamedFrom entry 'status', but object crm_account still declares a field status: that name is still in use, so no field was renamed away from it. ...`

## Acceptance notes

- **The key is inert until #30885.** Between this landing and the rename execution, an upgrade that meets `renamedFrom` does what it does today (additive sync). The describe, the docs row and the changeset each say so; the ledger row's note records the card's plan that #30884 refuses a declared rename by name until #30885 lands. That refusal is #30884's to build: until it lands, nothing refuses either.
- **Extension fields get the field half only.** `ObjectExtensionSchema.fields` parses `FieldSchema`, so an extension field may carry `renamedFrom` with its grammar judged, but the map half runs only in `ObjectSchema`'s refinement, where the whole field map is visible. The card scopes the checks to the object; no extension behaviour is added.
- **The grammar refusal names the entry, not the object or field.** `FieldSchema` sees one field at a time and `name` is optional; the issue path locates it. Every map-half refusal names all three.
- **Empty list:** `renamedFrom: []` parses (no rename declared). The card's minimal list does not refuse it, so this PR does not.
- **One ablation per rule** (each through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, anchor hit x1 to x0, restored, `git diff HEAD` empty after the run): grammar, repeat, live key and double claim each turned their pin red on the first run. The own-key ablation stayed green on its first run: the pin's `toContain("the field's own key")` also matched the shared prescription sentence, so the assertion was vacuous. The pin now asserts the reason clause, and the re-run ablation turned it red (`refuses the field's own key` failed, 1 of 11).
- **`Metadata-protocol:` line.** The claim carried `Metadata-protocol: none`; this body declares `added`, because AGENTS.md defines a new authorable key as `added` and `check-changeset-no-major` refuses `none` beside a changed `authorable-surface/` shard. Reported to the seat.
- `origin/main` moved 10 commits after the branch point; none touches `packages/spec`, `packages/metadata-core`, `packages/drivers/driver-sql`, `packages/metadata-protocol` or `content/docs` (only other cards' changesets and an ADR anchor), so the branch was not merged before opening.
